question: Should OpenClaw accept RFC 0018's opt-in readiness contract, including its activation trigger, required/advisory aggregation, subject identity package, and activation-scoped plugin provider boundary?
rationale: These choices define new configuration, endpoint, CLI, and plugin compatibility commitments; code review cannot determine the intended long-term public contract without maintainer direction.

options.title: Accept the proposed v1 boundary
options.body: Approve the opt-in contract and record the four requested decisions so the RFC can serve as the agreed implementation boundary.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Approve only the core condition model and defer plugin providers or subject identity until their compatibility commitments are separately reviewed.

options.title: Decline this direction
options.body: Keep the existing Gateway checker as the supported contract and close or replace the RFC with a smaller documented improvement.

recommendation.title: Accept the proposed v1 boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in contract and record the four requested decisions so the RFC can serve as the agreed implementation boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied RFC history makes this contributor the best available routing contact for clarifying the proposal, while the acceptance decision remains with repository maintainers.
